text:
alex_acme: Hey team — our mobile app started returning 401s to Redwood around 2024-11-05 14:30-14:40 UTC. The SDK just logs 'Unauthorized' and we can't find any request ids in our logs. What should we collect?

samir_support: Sorry about that. First quick checks — are you definitely sending the Authorization header as `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>`? Which SDK and exact version are you on?

alex_acme: iOS SDK v1.2.3, yes we set the header. We see the 401 in our UI but no x-rw-request-id or similar in our response logging.

olivia_oncall: Ok. The things that help most are: a) one raw SDK log capture from a single failed request (enable debug level briefly), b) a HAR or curl reproduction showing request and response headers, c) exact timestamp range + org/team id so we can search server logs.

samir_support: To enable debug on iOS quickly: `RWIClient.logLevel = .debug` then reproduce the failure once. The SDK usually emits a line like `RedwoodSDK DEBUG: request_id=abcd-1234 status=401`. If you don't see that, we'll rely on the HAR/curl + timestamps.

alex_acme: I enabled debug but the only lines I see are: `RedwoodSDK INFO: request failed status=401 message=Unauthorized`. No request_id.

samir_support: That's fine — please run this minimal curl from a machine in the same network as the app (so we can match IPs/time) and paste the full response headers. Use `-i` to include headers: 

```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"test trace"}'
```

Look for a header in the response named `x-rw-request-id` or `x-request-id`. If present, copy that value. If the header is missing, still attach the full response (status, headers, body).

olivia_oncall: For browser-based reproductions, capture a HAR: Chrome DevTools -> Network -> reproduce -> right click -> Save all as HAR with content. Attach the HAR. In HAR entries the request/response headers and timings help us correlate.

alex_acme: For mobile, where do we look for the id if the SDK logs it?

samir_support: iOS logs: look for `RedwoodSDK` tag in device logs (Console.app or device logs). Android logs: `RWI` tag in `adb logcat`. The SDK includes `request_id=<id>` when present. Also check the response headers at the network layer — some mobile networking libs surface headers separately.

olivia_oncall: Additional metadata we need in the ticket: org/team id (from Console), approximate user/customer id hitting endpoint, exact UTC time window (to the minute), and a sample request payload (you can redact user data). If you prefer, attach a debug bundle: we will give you a small upload token to send logs securely.

alex_acme: One more: how do we run a request that definitely returns the server-set headers so we can capture `x-rw-request-id`?

samir_support: Use the curl above and `-i`. Or run curl with `-D -` to print headers separately. Example: `curl -D - -X POST ...` Also you can pipe through `sed -n '1,20p'` to limit output. If your network strips custom headers, note that — include proxy or CDN details.

olivia_oncall: Once you attach one of: (1) HAR with the failing request, (2) curl run with `-i` showing headers, or (3) SDK debug logs with a request_id — we will correlate on our side and return a debug token and the trace id mapping. 

alex_acme: Copying logs and HAR now, attaching in a follow-up message. Thanks. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket #34567 created and attached to this thread. We will update when correlation is ready.
